children: The ‘AU Bank Bandra Colony’ branding will extend across station signage, ticketing areas, platforms and in-train displays, giving the bank a sustained presence on Mumbai Metro 3’s Aqua Line

AU Small Finance Bank (AU SFB) has secured exclusive three-year naming and station-wide branding rights for Bandra Colony Metro Station on Mumbai Metro 3’s Aqua Line. The association, secured through Times Innovative Media Limited (TIML), gives the bank visibility across station naming assets and multiple commuter touchpoints.

The station has been renamed ‘AU Bank Bandra Colony’. Located in Bandra East, close to the Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), the station also adjoins AU SFB’s upcoming head office, connecting the bank’s corporate base with a key commercial district and a busy urban transit corridor.

The initiative adds to AU SFB’s portfolio of high-visibility brand platforms. Its presence on television property Kaun Banega Crorepati has helped extend its national visibility, while the metro association takes the brand into Mumbai’s everyday commuting environment.

Mumbai remains an important market for the bank, given its position as a financial centre and the presence of major corporates, financial institutions and regulators. AU SFB currently operates 54 physical touchpoints across the city.

The branding covers several areas across the station, including entry and exit signage, digital station-name displays, route maps and roundels, ticketing areas, automated fare collection gates, escalators, concourses, platform screen doors and advertising units. The ‘AU Bank Bandra Colony’ identity also features on relevant in-train route maps and station indicators.
The bank has also integrated its banking propositions into the commuting environment, with personal loan and credit card communication placed across relevant passenger touchpoints.

According to the Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation (MMRC), Mumbai Metro 3’s Aqua Line recorded more than seven crore passenger journeys in its first year of full-route operations between Aarey JVLR and Cuffe Parade. The corridor connects several of Mumbai’s major commercial, financial and residential hubs.
